title: Peer/receipt Sender Behavior paragraph hard to parse
description: Location: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md, Peer/receipt Sender Behavior section, lines 304-306. Issue: The paragraph is a single dense run-on sentence with nested conditional logic: 'if Chat.receiptSharing is present for the relevant Chat, that value is used; otherwise the account-level PresenceStatus.receiptSharing applies ... If the effective preference is false, the server MUST NOT invoke Peer/receipt.' The term 'effective preference' is introduced mid-sentence without prior definition, making it easy to misread. An implementor scanning for the MUST rule has to parse through two conditional branches before reaching the normative requirement. Suggested fix: introduce 'effective preference' as a defined term at the start ('The effective receipt-sharing preference is Chat.receiptSharing if present for the relevant Chat, otherwise PresenceStatus.receiptSharing.'), then state the MUST rule in a separate sentence referencing that term.
close_reason: Opinion: SEC7 labeled this; logic is correct and implementable
